paper_title: First results of the CERN Resonant WISP Search (CROWS)
coupling_convention: kinetic mixing parameter chi, dimensionless, as plotted on y-axis
notes: CROWS is a microwave light-shining-through-wall experiment probing both ALPs (AxionPhoton, g=4.5e-8 GeV^-1 at 7.2 ueV) and hidden sector photons (DarkPhoton, chi=4.1e-9 at 10.8 ueV). Chose DarkPhoton per hint and abstract emphasis (previously unexplored region). Only single best-sensitivity text values available; full exclusion curves are in Figs 13/14 but numerical data not tabulated. Not a haloscope, so no local DM density. 95% CL. If AxionPhoton is desired, the ALP point is [7.2e-6, 4.5e-8] GeV^-1 (most sensitive) with wideband g=9.9e-8 GeV^-1. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.72, 32)) | Vision: FIG. 14, light-shining-through-wall microwave search for Hidden Sector Photons (HSP = dark photon). y-axis is kinetic mixing chi (dimensionless), x-axis HSP mass in eV. Confidence level 95%. The resonant dip minimum (chi=4.1e-9 at m=10.8 ueV=1.08e-5 eV) is explicitly annotated on the plot and used to calibrate the trace. The excluded blue region has a broad diagonal upper-left edge that narrows into a sharp resonant spike; boundary sampled densely around the spike. Left/right arms of the V are somewhat symmetric about the resonant frequency. Values right of the dip are more approximate due to overlap with adjacent grey (XENON10) region. | Calibration: No calibration needed (spot-check verify/stage2 raw_ratio=1.75 snapped to identity)
